answer: A bond-backed entry system gives a new identity weight only after it locks a 50-unit bond that no other account can share or reuse. The identity first spends 14 days in haven with zero weight, then crosses a canyon by passing three independent audits, and its audit score must reach a summit of 90 points before any weight is granted. An operator running 100 fakes must therefore lock 5,000 units, wait 1,400 separate days, and pass 300 audits, since bonds, waiting time, and audits never transfer between accounts.
